source.title: Enhancing Neural Training via a Correlated Dynamics Model
source.authors: J. Brokman; Roy Betser; Rotem Turjeman; Tom Berkov; Ido Cohen; G. Gilboa

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares held-out accuracy after CMD modeling or embedding with baseline training, using a different intervention from the claim versions. It does not test the versions’ specified mechanisms or conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports natural-image test accuracy for CMD training methods against baseline SGD and reports train/validation landscape differences. Its results do not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, adaptive optimizers against SGD, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal. The CMD accuracy comparisons are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: Table 2 incidentally tests V4 in a ResNet18/CIFAR10 setting: baseline Adam reaches 89.59% test accuracy versus 90.68–91.29% for SGD variants. Appendix D specifies a shared learning rate of 0.05 and 150 epochs, without an optimizer-specific tuning search. The CMD comparisons themselves test none of the versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that CMD compactly models correlated training dynamics, improves accuracy over baseline training in their experiments, and reduces federated-learning communication overhead while maintaining performance.
record.recipe_differences: CMD models or embeds correlated parameter trajectories during training; it is not the original study methods or interventions described in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy varies across model and dataset settings; CMD mode count and sampling choices are also studied, with test accuracy described as close to invariant to mode count and robust across sampled subsets and random initializations.

fits_no_version.finding: Online CMD increases mean CIFAR10 accuracy relative to the corresponding baseline across the six Table 1 architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Online CMD can improve held-out image-classification accuracy in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Online CMD increases mean accuracy within each Table 2 optimizer condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CMD can improve ResNet18/CIFAR10 accuracy when applied alongside SGD variants or Adam.

fits_no_version.finding: CMD improves reported mean accuracy in the additional CIFAR100, TinyImageNet, and federated CIFAR10 comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CMD can improve accuracy across additional image-classification settings and reduce federated communication volume.

record.problems: The results concern CMD’s modeled or embedded training dynamics, not the claim versions’ specified mechanisms. Several results compare methods on test accuracy without reporting the training error or train-test gap. The text does not provide numerical values for some figure-only comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Other CMD variants and additional comparisons are described in tables and figures, but omitted to keep rows focused on reported baseline-versus-CMD test accuracy. This includes post-hoc/embedded comparisons, additional regularizers EMA and SWA, and CMD hyperparameter sensitivity plots (Tables 2, 4, 9, 10; Figures 12–14, 19). The paper’s validation-accuracy and landscape observations are not extracted as rows because they are figure/text descriptions of landscape behavior rather than measurements named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization under matched architectures and training recipes.
Width sweeps, interpolation thresholds, and test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and local-connectivity or initialization comparisons.
Optimizer-specific learning-rate tuning, broader hyperparameter searches, matched training performance, language benchmarks, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removal of memorized versus random training examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: Extract cross-optimizer baseline comparisons: Adam 89.59% ± 0.43 versus SGD 90.68% ± 0.29, momentum SGD 90.91% ± 0.52, and momentum SGD with cosine scheduling 91.29% ± 0.23. All use learning rate 0.05 and 150 epochs; no optimizer-specific tuning search is reported.
missing.locator: Table 2, baseline column; Appendix D, Table 2 implementation details

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks the cross-optimizer information in Table 2. Its within-optimizer CMD contrasts remain outside all versions. Landscape visualizations do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps. No files or external sources were accessed.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the stated local-connectivity comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons under the stated tuning regimes and recovery conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout comparisons across training-set sizes and dropout strengths.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing and retraining on memorized examples versus random examples.
